key_insight: Optimal control enables simulated 12-ns controlled-Z gates between directly coupled, tunable transmons with intrinsic errors near 2×10⁻⁵ while identifying noise-resilient operating regimes.
engineering_relevance: Smooth flux pulses and transmon-asymmetry tuning offer practical routes to balance gate speed, fidelity, and robustness while potentially reducing recalibration overhead.
method: Optimize smooth, single-shot flux pulses while accounting for intrinsic Hamiltonian errors, relaxation, and dephasing.
Model fast electronics-induced dephasing and slow 1/f flux noise using published experimental measurements.
Identify dephasing sweet spots and exploit transmon asymmetry to improve noise resilience.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 12-ns gates near an 11.6-ns theoretical speed limit, intrinsic errors around 2×10⁻⁵, and noise models calibrated against published measurements.
watch_item: The reported intrinsic error is not the total error under decoherence, and performance requires validation on experimental hardware.
paper_title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. I. Intrinsic errors and decoherence
